subject: Mixed (Real Weightage)
description: 100 questions following the real PGP-CET 2025 subject weightage. Mix: 74 easy / 26 medium / 0 hard. Tier is relative: the easy third of the 60 papers by average question difficulty. Every question cites its source.

questions.question: Salbutamol relieves asthma by:

options.B: Stimulating beta-2 adrenergic receptors causing bronchodilatation

questions.explanation: Side effects: tremor, tachycardia, hypokalaemia.

questions.question: The anterior cruciate ligament prevents:

questions.explanation: ACL arises from the posteromedial aspect of the lateral femoral condyle and inserts into the anterior intercondylar area.

questions.question: Kwashiorkor is caused mainly by deficiency of:
questions.explanation: Marasmus is severe energy deficiency with wasting; kwashiorkor has oedema, skin lesions and fatty liver.

questions.question: Anti-embolism stockings are used to:

questions.question: A patient with a fractured neck of femur typically presents with a limb that is:
questions.explanation: Posterior hip dislocation: shortened, flexed, adducted and internally rotated.

questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: The olfactory nerve is cranial nerve number:
questions.explanation: Optic II, oculomotor III, trochlear IV, trigeminal V, abducens VI.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: When climbing stairs with crutches, the correct sequence is:

options.A: Up with the bad, down with the good
options.C: Up with the good, down with the bad

questions.explanation: Going up the stronger leg leads, then crutches and weaker leg; going down the crutches and weaker leg lead.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Acute gout is best treated with:
questions.explanation: Allopurinol is for prophylaxis between attacks, not started during an acute attack.

questions.question: A dipeptide, formed from two amino acids, contains how many peptide bonds?
questions.explanation: A dipeptide has two amino acids joined by exactly one peptide bond — a common point of confusion, since it's easy to assume 'two amino acids' implies 'two bonds.'

questions.sourceChapter: Proteins and Amino Acids — Peptide Bond
questions.subject: Biochemistry

questions.question: An essential fatty acid is:
questions.explanation: Linoleic (omega-6) and alpha-linolenic (omega-3) acids must be obtained from the diet.

questions.subject: Biochemistry

questions.question: Cysticercosis in humans is most commonly acquired by:

options.B: Eating undercooked pork ('measly pork') or ingesting contaminated vegetables/food carrying Taenia solium eggs

questions.explanation: Cysticercosis is infection by the larval stage of Taenia solium (the pork tapeworm). Humans acquire it by eating undercooked ('measly') pork containing larval cysts, by ingesting food/vegetables contaminated with eggs, or occasionally by autoinfection.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: Rehabilitation of a patient after stroke is an example of:
questions.explanation: Tertiary prevention limits disability and restores function.

questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: The karyotype in Turner syndrome is:
questions.explanation: Short stature, webbed neck, primary amenorrhoea. Klinefelter is 47,XXY.

questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: In acute severe asthma which finding indicates life-threatening disease?

options.B: A silent chest, cyanosis or exhaustion

questions.explanation: A silent chest means very little air entry.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: The core treatment for knee osteoarthritis is:

options.D: Exercise therapy, education and weight management

questions.explanation: Quadriceps strengthening and aerobic activity reduce pain.

questions.question: Lateral epicondylitis most commonly involves the tendon of:
questions.explanation: Overuse is degenerative (tendinosis) rather than inflammatory.

questions.question: Which of the following is a good electrical conductor?
questions.explanation: Insulators: rubber, glass, plastic, dry air.

questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Which finding in a patient with low back pain requires URGENT referral?

options.B: New bladder or bowel dysfunction with saddle anaesthesia

questions.explanation: Other red flags: progressive neurological deficit, fever, weight loss, history of cancer, trauma.

questions.question: A cock-up (wrist extension) splint is indicated in:

questions.question: The audible frequency range of the normal human ear is about:
questions.explanation: Ultrasound is above 20 kHz.

questions.question: The normal carrying angle of the elbow in adults is about:
questions.explanation: It is formed by the long axes of the arm and forearm in the anatomical position; valgus > 15° is cubitus valgus.

questions.question: On a 0–4 grading scale, a deep tendon reflex graded 2+ is:

questions.question: Cardiac output is the product of:

questions.question: Idiopathic (hereditary) haemochromatosis is characterised by a classic triad of pigmentary liver cirrhosis, skin pigmentation, and:

options.A: Pancreatic damage resulting in diabetes mellitus ('bronze diabetes')

questions.explanation: Hereditary haemochromatosis is characterised by a triad: pigmentary liver cirrhosis, pancreatic damage causing diabetes mellitus, and skin pigmentation — earning it the nickname 'bronze diabetes' based on the latter two features.

questions.question: The hook-like projection near the base of which carpal bone gives attachment to the flexor retinaculum?
questions.explanation: The hamate is wedge-shaped with a hook projecting from the distal part of its palmar surface; the tip of the hook gives attachment to the flexor retinaculum, and its medial side gives origin to flexor digiti minimi and opponens digiti minimi.
questions.sourceBook: BD Chaurasia's Human Anatomy — Upper Limb
questions.sourceChapter: Bones of the Upper Limb — Carpal Bones
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: A transient ischaemic attack (TIA) is characterised by:

options.A: Focal neurological deficit resolving completely within 24 hours (usually minutes)

questions.explanation: TIAs are a warning of impending stroke.

questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: A patient with recurrent anterior shoulder dislocation will resist the examiner's movement of the arm into:
questions.explanation: This is the apprehension test.

questions.question: The most common level of lumbar disc prolapse is:

questions.question: The ‘pull test’ in Parkinson's disease evaluates:

questions.question: Pronation of the forearm is performed mainly by:
questions.explanation: Median nerve supply (anterior interosseous for pronator quadratus).

questions.question: Why is establishing a 1-RM (single maximum effort) considered inappropriate for certain patient populations, such as those with osteoporosis or cardiovascular pathology?

options.A: It takes too long to administer in a clinical setting
options.B: It requires a single maximal effort, which carries risk for patients with joint impairments, healing soft tissue, osteoporosis, or cardiovascular pathology
options.C: It is only valid for measuring endurance, not strength
options.D: It cannot be performed using free weights

questions.explanation: A 1-RM test requires the patient to exert one true maximal effort, which is unsafe for patients with joint impairments, those recovering from or at risk of soft tissue injury, or those with osteoporosis or cardiovascular pathology — alternative methods (e.g. multiple-RM formulas, dynamometry, percentage of body weight) are used instead for these patients.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 6: Resistance Exercise — Repetition Maximum, Precautions
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: The normal range of elbow flexion is about:
questions.explanation: Soft tissue approximation limits flexion; extension 0° (hard end feel).

questions.question: The normal glomerular filtration rate in a healthy adult is about:

questions.question: Humidification of inspired oxygen helps by:

options.B: Reducing the viscosity of secretions and preventing mucosal drying

questions.explanation: Essential for patients on high-flow oxygen or with artificial airways.

questions.question: An ankle–foot orthosis is MOST appropriately used for:

questions.question: A body is in static equilibrium when:

options.B: It is moving at high speed
options.C: The sum of all forces and the sum of all torques acting on it equals zero

questions.question: For a diagnosis of significant sleep apnoea, apnoeic episodes (cessation of airflow for 10+ seconds) typically must number at least how many per hour of sleep?

questions.question: WHO recommends exclusive breastfeeding for the first:

questions.question: The Gestalt psychologists' core principle, 'the whole is more than the sum of its parts,' means that:

options.A: Organized perceptual experience has properties that cannot be predicted from simply analysing its individual components
options.B: Larger objects are always perceived more accurately than small ones
options.C: Perception is entirely determined by the number of sensory receptors involved
options.D: Only visual perception follows organizational principles, not other senses

questions.explanation: The central Gestalt idea is that organized perceptual experience has emergent properties not predictable from a simple analysis of its component sensations — perception involves active organization, not just addition of individual sensory 'atoms'.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology
questions.sourceChapter: Sensory Processes and Perception — Organization in Perception

questions.question: 'ROWS' (Rule Out Worst-case Scenario) as a clinical strategy is best illustrated by which example?

options.A: Assuming pleuritic chest pain and breathlessness is always a pulled muscle
options.B: Actively investigating for pulmonary embolism in a patient presenting with pleuritic chest pain and breathlessness, because missing it could be fatal
options.C: Ignoring red flag symptoms in back pain to save time
options.D: Only used for patients over 65 years old

questions.explanation: ROWS forces clinicians to actively consider and rule out serious, potentially fatal diagnoses that can present with common symptoms — the classic textbook example is investigating for pulmonary embolism in a patient with pleuritic chest pain and breathlessness.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine
